svg.text: No stack, no heap: ownership resolved at compile time, values live in registers (plus optional fixed RAM and ROM)
Compiler rejects anything needing runtime memory management: recursion, unbounded growth, dynamic allocation. Nothing is left to manage at runtime.
No primary stack • No managed heap • No dynamic allocation • Fixed, known-at-compile-time layout
add • sub • mul • compare • shift • logic
Each register has one owner; it is reused when that owner's scope ends (decided at compile time)
Locals of inlined functions become registers – there are no call frames
Rust-style ownership is enforced at compile time only – no runtime checks, no allocator, no GC on this target
HOW THE FULL FUSION MODEL MAPS DOWN
Fixed-capacity slots, sized at compile time
ROM table; string ID kept in a register
Only if all N objects fit in registers
Ownership by default; manual or GC if configured
Data Stacks become static regions sized at compile time
No RAM allocation at all; input → working → output
Conceptual diagram – layouts vary by target chip.
